sources.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract; PDF definitions 25/28 and §§3.4–3.5 selected passages, not full 64-page proof audit.
sources.comparison: Intervention-preserving abstractions, mediation and path patching precede our certificate. Identified mathematical models and independently grounded physical ports are different evidence situations.

sources.title: Inducing Causal Structure for Interpretable Neural Networks
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract and method description only.
sources.comparison: Interchange training aligns internal representations to causal variables; zero loss has a conditional abstraction guarantee. Not our bodily-familiarity endpoint.

sources.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
sources.read_scope: Author text §3, noising/denoising, scope, minimality and backup-behavior passages.
sources.comparison: Necessary and sufficient perturbation evidence need not coincide; path-specific interventions and compensating backup mechanisms are established concerns.

sources.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
sources.read_scope: Author abstract only; experiments not reanalyzed.
sources.comparison: Metrics and corruption choices affect localization; no claim of our method outperforming theirs is justified.

sources.title: Cortical mechanisms of action selection: the affordance competition hypothesis
sources.read_scope: Author PDF abstract and competition-model passages, pp. 5–6; not all cited neural experiments or supplements.
sources.comparison: Parallel action options, mutual inhibition and biased selection have longstanding antecedents. A model-specific choice threshold is not a basal experience threshold.

sources.title: Sense of control depends on fluency of action selection, not motor performance
sources.read_scope: Repository abstract; original PDF methods, PCE/NCE comparison, results and discussion excerpts; supplements not reviewed.
sources.comparison: Compatibility effects on control ratings dissociate from response performance. Selection fluency here is inferred from priming, not a verified count of live A3O policy tokens.

sources.title: The Rubber Hand Illusion: Feeling of Ownership and Proprioceptive Drift Do Not Go Hand in Hand
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract, discussion and conclusion; no new data analysis.
sources.comparison: Spatial drift cannot simply identify ownership in their paradigm; it does not validate a retentive bodily-familiarity measure.

sources.title: Moving a Rubber Hand that Feels Like Your Own: A Dissociation of Ownership and Agency
sources.read_scope: Publisher hypothesis, factorial active/passive and congruence results, and double-dissociation conclusion; not complete raw-data audit.
sources.comparison: Ownership/agency dissociation is empirical prior work. Neither axis is independently established as our familiar bodily H.

sources.title: Self-healing codes: How stable neural populations can track continually reconfiguring neural representations
sources.read_scope: Repository abstract and original PDF pp. 1–2, background/readout description; later model proofs and code not rerun.
sources.comparison: Adaptive readers can track changing population codes. Stable output does not guarantee an unchanged code/reader; this is not a natural-source area-3a rescue experiment.

sources.title: Two fluency heuristics (and how to tell them apart)
sources.read_scope: Primary publisher indexed abstract only; direct full-page access failed twice.
sources.comparison: Fluency-related familiarity and attribution already have a research literature. Scope is recognition familiarity, not current bodily mineness; detailed experiments and priority were not assessed.

sources.title: Am I seeing myself, my friend or a stranger? The role of personal familiarity in visual distinction of body identities in the human brain
sources.comparison: Self, personally familiar other and unfamiliar body images were compared. Visual identity familiarity is a nearby construct, not retentive enactment or validated H.

sources.title: Group Testing: An Information Theory Perspective
sources.read_scope: Author abstract only; mathematical background reference, no exact theorem-priority determination.
sources.comparison: Binary pooled OR testing and information bounds are established. SCU already explicitly credits separating-system and cover-free antecedents; no new general group-testing bound is claimed.
